answer: Resist sybils with anchored trust-graph walks: a candidate's influence equals how often short random walks from a trusted seed set land on it, so only identities reached through real vouching chains gain weight. An ocean of puppet accounts buys almost nothing, each forged edge costs only copper yet adds negligible routing mass toward any single fake. The nadir trick, flooding thousands of fakes cheaply, fails because influence is per-region, not per-account; defeating it means corrupting many edges near the honest core, which in time and detection risk costs more than being honest.
